lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to start by asking about the child you're claiming for.

**First, let me ask about the child's age:**

How old is the child (or children) you're asking about? 

- Are they **under 16**?
- Are they **16 to 19 years old**?
- Or are they **20 or over**?

Please let me know the age of each child you want to claim Child Benefit for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19 years old, I need to check additional requirements. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check Alex's education or training status. For young people aged 16-19, they need to be in approved education or training, or have recently left education.

**Which of these applies to Alex?**

1. **He is currently in approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education, or approved vocational training)

2. **He recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)

3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which situation describes Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is currently in education studying for his A-levels at sixth form college. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels are an approved non-advanced qualification. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

**1. Is Alex's A-level course full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - which most sixth form A-level courses are)

**2. Is this education funded by an employer or part of an agreement for a future job with an employer?** (This would typically be something like an apprenticeship with guaranteed employment)

Could you confirm these details about Alex's A-level studies?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a full-time course at sixth form - he's there during normal school hours throughout the week. And no, it's not funded by an employer or anything like that - it's just regular sixth form education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's helpful. A-levels at sixth form are approved non-advanced education, and since it's full-time (not employer-funded), Alex meets the education requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week (or is he not in paid work at all)?**

Children aged 16 and over who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible for Child Benefit, even if they're in education.

What's Alex's work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex does work quite a bit - he has a part-time job at the local supermarket and works full-time hours there alongside his studies. He's working more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for letting me know. This is an important detail.

Since Alex is working 24 hours or more per week, let me navigate to the outcome for this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex at this time.

**Here's why:**

While Alex is 17 and studying A-levels at sixth form college (which is approved non-advanced education), he is working more than 24 hours per week at his supermarket job. Under UK Child Benefit rules, **children aged 16 or over who work 24 or more hours per week are not eligible for Child Benefit**, even if they are still in approved education or training.

**Important information:**

- Child Benefit stops when a child aged 16 or over starts paid work for 24+ hours per week
- This applies even though Alex is still in full-time education

**What you can do:**

If Alex's work situation changes in the future and he reduces his hours to less than 24 per week while continuing his education, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to contact HMRC to restart your claim if that happens.

I understand this may be disappointing news, especially since Alex is balancing both education and significant work commitments. If you have any questions about this decision or need clarification, please let me know.
